title: Hire year
prompt: Show each employee's name and the year they were hired, as hire_year. Replace the ___.
starterSql:
SELECT name, strftime('___', hire_date) AS hire_year
FROM employees;

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT name, strftime('%Y', hire_date) AS hire_year FROM employees;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name, strftime('%m', hire_date) AS hire_year FROM employees;
SELECT name, hire_date AS hire_year FROM employees;

title: Order month
prompt: Show each order's id and its year and month like 2024-01, as order_month.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT id, strftime('%Y-%m', order_date) AS order_month FROM orders;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT id, strftime('%Y', order_date) AS order_month FROM orders;
SELECT id, strftime('%m', order_date) AS order_month FROM orders;

title: Days since signup
prompt: Show each user's username and how many days after 2024-01-01 they signed up, as days_after. The result should be a whole number.
hints: Subtract julianday values, and CAST to INTEGER.
solutions: SELECT username, CAST(julianday(signup_date) - julianday('2024-01-01') AS INTEGER) AS days_after FROM users;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT username, CAST(julianday('2024-01-01') - julianday(signup_date) AS INTEGER) AS days_after FROM users;
SELECT username, signup_date AS days_after FROM users;

title: Next day
prompt: Show each reading's reading_date and the day after it, as next_day.
solutions: SELECT reading_date, date(reading_date, '+1 day') AS next_day FROM readings;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT reading_date, date(reading_date, '-1 day') AS next_day FROM readings;
SELECT reading_date, reading_date + 1 AS next_day FROM readings;

title: Across a month end
prompt: Show each reading's reading_date and the day before it, as previous_day. The hidden test crosses a month boundary.
solutions: SELECT reading_date, date(reading_date, '-1 day') AS previous_day FROM readings;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT reading_date, reading_date - 1 AS previous_day FROM readings;
SELECT reading_date, date(reading_date, '-1 month') AS previous_day FROM readings;

title: Fix the function
prompt: This should show each employee's name and hire year as hire_year, but SQLite has no YEAR function. Fix it.
starterSql:
SELECT name, YEAR(hire_date) AS hire_year
FROM employees;

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT name, strftime('%Y', hire_date) AS hire_year FROM employees;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name, hire_date AS hire_year FROM employees;
SELECT name, strftime('%y', hire_date) AS hire_year FROM employees;

title: February orders
prompt: Show the id and order_date of orders placed in February of any year. strftime returns text, so compare with '02'.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT id, order_date FROM orders WHERE strftime('%m', order_date) = '02';

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT id, order_date FROM orders WHERE strftime('%m', order_date) = 2;
SELECT id, order_date FROM orders WHERE order_date = '2024-02';

title: Tenure at year end
prompt: Show each employee's name and full years employed by 2024-12-31, as tenure_years. Divide the days by 365.25, then CAST to INTEGER. Only include hires before 2022.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT name, CAST((julianday('2024-12-31') - julianday(hire_date)) / 365.25 AS INTEGER) AS tenure_years FROM employees WHERE hire_date < '2022-01-01';

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name, CAST((julianday('2024-12-31') - julianday(hire_date)) / 365.25 AS INTEGER) AS tenure_years FROM employees;
SELECT name, CAST(julianday('2024-12-31') - julianday(hire_date) AS INTEGER) AS tenure_years FROM employees WHERE hire_date < '2022-01-01';
